reviewedPolicy.conclusion: Only ready, nonloading, error-free catalogue association is used. Exact path-component matching rejects malformed or component-relative paths and prefix lookalikes; it does not resolve filesystem aliases. One matching archive takes precedence; conflicting archives yield no association. Recovery only records related backup history, independent of original-path existence or recovery availability.

App.openRow and App.recover guard only kind=archive. A recovery association leaves the prior native-session/connection eligibility flow intact, including explicit ordinary open/reconnect. It does not choose a backup, restore anything, change cwd or send a prompt.

ThreadView current catalogue recheck only adds the archive guard to its existing recovery path. Retained handlers distinguish archive from recovery; existing active/request ownership and ordinary history-failure paths remain. The normal reconnect action survives the recovery hint.

ArchivedWorkLocationNotice recovery branch first renders the unmodified ErrorNotice fallback including title/message/detail/children, then a separate management hint. archiveHandled suppresses only duplicate management and still returns the fallback for recovery. Existing archive replacement behavior is retained.

EmptyState passes remembered diagnostic cwd separately from a work grant. ComposerWorkNotice only attaches guidance to the existing work-load/reconnect failure classes; other errors remain ordinary. Recovery keeps work-settings error/retry and exact unsent text/path. No automatic use or cwd migration.

Click checks mounted/active/current cwd/current catalogue source before opening shared management with target=null. Multiple backups remain distinct choices; no implicit recovery selection. Loading/error/replaced catalogue retires old hints and rejects old handlers.

effectiveCounterexample.scenario: Prepare a recovery copy, cancel deletion, then explicitly restore the still-retained archive to its original directory. The recovery record persists and must not prevent that now-normal history connection.
